newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea gives go-ahead to futures association.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea gives go-ahead to futures association.

text.p: South Korea's finance minister has approved the establishment of the Korea Futures Association (KFA) and a promotional organisation to develop the country's first dedicated futures exchange, the KFA's head said on Friday.

"We, the newly licensed futures brokers, have founded the Korea Futures Association (KFA) and an organisation of promoters to develop the country's own futures exchange," Bae Jeong-hwan, chairman of the KFA and head of the promotional organisation, told Reuters.
Bae is also president of futures broker Korea Commodity Inc.
Last November, the Finance Ministry gave approval for 35 companies to operate as futures brokers on both domestic and overseas exchanges.

Bae said the new futures exchange was expected to be established in October, 1998 and will list commodities and financial instruments, but not stock index futures, which are already traded on the Korea Stock Exchnage.

The futures contracts to be listed on the exchange have not yet been confirmed, although gold, three-year corporate bonds, won-dollar futures and certificates of deposit are under consideration, industry sources said.
The exchange's new promotional organisation will design the contracts and set up the exchange's trading system, Bae said.
There are eight members of the promotional organisation from whose ranks the board of directors of the KFA are drawn.

The eight firms include: Korea Commodity Inc, Tong Yang Futures Co Ltd, the Korea Development Bank, Kookmin Bank, Daewoo Securities Co Ltd, Daeyoo Securities Co Ltd, Korea Development Leasing Co Ltd and Kyobo Life Insurance Co Ltd.
